description: This chapter of NASA's State-of-the-Art of Small Spacecraft Technology report surveys the ground segment that small satellite missions rely on: ground system architectures, frequency selection and licensing, NASA's Near Space Network and Deep Space Network and partner networks, commercial ground segment as a service, space relay and low-latency short-burst relay providers, ground station components and software, mission and science operations centres, end-to-end compatibility testing, cyber security and optical ground stations. The NASA Small Spacecraft Systems Virtual Institute publishes the report, and this chapter was updated on 11 May 2026 with a downloadable PDF. Coverage is worldwide providers and technologies, with a US focus. Format and access: a free web chapter with PDF, glossary and references. Licence: NASA public content. Caveats: it is a technology survey that names providers and capabilities but does not give station coordinates or capacity data as a table file, and a round 1 screen set it aside as general information. It describes the ground infrastructure dependencies of space services for capacity planning and resilience studies. Related catalogue records are the Landsat Ground Network and the SatNOGS database.
